diagnosis.summary: payment-service is returning 5xx on every request and its end-to-end latency has surged from 4.5 ms to 4419 ms at the 95th percentile. order-service, which calls payment-service on every order, is seeing 95 dependency errors per minute and a 5xx rate of 40.95% against a baseline of zero. Both services are severely degraded.
diagnosis.root_cause: A failure within payment-service that produces 100% 5xx responses and extreme end-to-end latency is the most likely root cause. Notably, payment-service's lambda_duration_ms_mean rose only from 0.59 ms to 1.72 ms, while its p95 end-to-end latency is 4419 ms, indicating the time is not spent inside the handler body itself.
evidence: payment-service error_rate_5xx is currently 1.0 (100%) against a baseline of 0, meaning every request is failing.
payment-service p95 end-to-end latency rose from 4.5 ms to 4419.4 ms, roughly a 981x increase, and p50 latency rose from 0.038 ms to 4417.97 ms.
payment-service lambda_duration_ms_mean is 1.72 ms (up from 0.59 ms baseline), far below the 4419 ms end-to-end latency, showing the handler body itself is not where the time is being spent.

order-service dependency_error_count is 95 per minute (baseline 0), and dependency_latency_ms_p95 is 4434.93 ms against a baseline of 22.15 ms, a 200x rise that closely matches payment-service's own p95 latency of 4419.4 ms.
order-service error_rate_5xx is 40.95% (baseline 0) and p95 latency rose from 25.06 ms to 4436.70 ms, approximately a 177x increase, with p99 latency rising from 30.01 ms to 4439.26 ms.
recommended_actions: Inspect payment-service CloudWatch Logs at /aws/lambda/anomalypulse-payment for errors or exceptions, focusing on what is consuming time outside the handler body given the gap between lambda_duration_ms_mean and end-to-end latency.
Check payment-service lambda_throttle_count in CloudWatch to determine whether Lambda throttling is contributing to failures; if so, configure reserved concurrency for payment-service.
Do not add retries to order-service's call to payment-service while payment-service is failing, as each retry would add more invocations and extend wait times for clients.
After identifying and fixing the payment-service issue, recheck payment-service error_rate_5xx and order-service dependency_error_count to confirm recovery.
Verify that GET requests to order-service remain unaffected, since only POST /orders invokes payment-service, to scope the customer impact accurately.
